speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with probable concurrent tracheomalacia.

The combination of stridor that worsens with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting, is classic for laryngomalacia. Given the wheezing component, I suspect concurrent tracheomalacia; please have the child undergo a flexible laryngoscopy to visualize the glottis.
